correctness.rationale: For each k≥1, a length-(2k+1) circularly k-universal word has k greedy mixed binary arches of combined length at least 2k, hence k disjoint unlike edges. Conversely a near-perfect matching of unlike cycle edges supplies a rotation with k two-letter arches. The transition XOR vector has even one-count and odd zero-count; deleting zero-edges yields disjoint paths. The matching sum (n-s+o)/2 reaches k iff exactly one interzero one-edge run is even. The unique even block roots the sequence; H(z)/(1-G(z)^2)=z(1-z^2)/(1-2z^2) yields 2^(k-1) rooted sequences for n=2k+1, n edge choices, two binary lifts. Repetition would multiply the unique exceptional block, proving primitivity. Greedy arch enumeration at fixed cut gives (k+2)2^k, yielding the rescued count. The n=3 endpoint and k=1 are included; n=1 and even n are expressly excluded. Independent finite checks of all binary words n≤16 and 6400 seeded larger samples passed; no finite extrapolation is used.

value.rationale: The parameter n=2k+1 is the first possible odd length allowing k binary-rich arches, so it is a natural minimal-slack boundary for circular universality. Exact labeled extremizers, the transition-vector parity defect, their universal primitivity, the 2^k necklace count and the (k-1)2^k fixed-cut rescue count give a complete structural and orbit classification useful in cyclic sequence design and universality counting. Prior linear counts and per-word circular algorithms do not provide these orbit conclusions without a new structural argument; the value does not depend on any unproved downstream theorem.
